title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation: Scalable Framework for Active-RAG Variant 8
abstract: We present Active-RAG (Variant 8), an advanced framework designed for active retrieval augmented generation. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, Active-RAG extends Dense Retrieval to enhance query grounding. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.

Abstract: We present Active-RAG (Variant 8), an advanced framework designed for active retrieval augmented generation. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, Active-RAG extends Dense Retrieval to enhance query grounding. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.
Introduction: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently generate hallucinated or ungrounded assertions when operating on specialized domains. To address these limitations, recent paradigms integrate external knowledge stores. Our proposed system, Active-RAG, directly addresses these challenges by introducing structured relational inductive biases. Specifically, Active-RAG extends Dense Retrieval, mitigating known factuality degradation.
Methodology: The architecture of Active-RAG consists of three core components: hierarchical retrieval, multi-scale verification, and grounded generation. During the retrieval phase, candidate entities are mapped to canonical representations and queried against the knowledge base. We demonstrate that Active-RAG extends Dense Retrieval with high confidence (0.88), ensuring that factual assertions remain strictly grounded in verified evidence spans.
Experiments and Evaluation: We evaluate Active-RAG on standard public benchmarks including BIRD-Dev, Spider-Test, GDPR, and CIVIL QA datasets. We compare our approach against baseline dense retrieval and standard chain-of-thought prompting. Our empirical results confirm that Active-RAG achieves superior precision and recall on Query Grounding, outperforming baseline methods by an average of 14.2% in factual accuracy.
Conclusion: In this paper, we introduced Active-RAG for active retrieval augmented generation. By ensuring Active-RAG extends Dense Retrieval, our framework achieves reliable, verifiable reasoning. Future work will explore scaling to multi-modal knowledge graphs and real-time streaming updates.
